heading.en: Do not count the overlap twice

hook.en: In a class, 20 students like cricket and 15 like football. Are there 35 students who like a sport? Not if some like both.
hook.kn: ತರಗತಿಯಲ್ಲಿ 20 ವಿದ್ಯಾರ್ಥಿಗಳಿಗೆ ಕ್ರಿಕೆಟ್, 15 ಮಂದಿಗೆ ಫುಟ್‌ಬಾಲ್ ಇಷ್ಟ. ಕ್ರೀಡೆ ಇಷ್ಟಪಡುವವರು 35 ಮಂದಿಯೇ? ಕೆಲವರಿಗೆ ಎರಡೂ ಇಷ್ಟವಾದರೆ ಅಲ್ಲ.

body.en: For any two events, $P(A \cup B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A \cap B)$: the overlap is counted twice in $P(A) + P(B)$, so we subtract it once. If A and B are mutually exclusive, $P(A \cap B) = 0$ and $P(A \cup B) = P(A) + P(B)$.
body.kn: P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A ∩ B). ಪರಸ್ಪರ ವರ್ಜಿತ ಘಟನೆಗಳಿಗೆ ಕೊನೆಯ ಪದ ಶೂನ್ಯ.

narration.en: P of A or B equals P of A plus P of B minus P of A and B. For mutually exclusive events the last term is zero.
narration.kn: P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A ∩ B). ಪರಸ್ಪರ ವರ್ಜಿತ ಘಟನೆಗಳಿಗೆ ಕೊನೆಯ ಪದ ಶೂನ್ಯ.

blocks.formula: P(A \cup B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A \cap B)

body.en: A and $A'$ are mutually exclusive and exhaustive, so $P(A') = 1 - P(A)$. Questions about "at least one" are usually easiest through the complement: P(at least one) = 1 − P(none).
body.kn: P(A ಅಲ್ಲ) = 1 − P(A). "ಕನಿಷ್ಠ ಒಂದು" ಎಂಬ ಪ್ರಶ್ನೆಗಳಿಗೆ 1 − P(ಯಾವುದೂ ಇಲ್ಲ) ಬಳಸಿ.

narration.en: The probability of not A is one minus the probability of A. For at least one, find the chance of none and subtract from one.
narration.kn: P(A ಅಲ್ಲ) = 1 − P(A). "ಕನಿಷ್ಠ ಒಂದು" ಎಂಬ ಪ್ರಶ್ನೆಗಳಿಗೆ 1 − P(ಯಾವುದೂ ಇಲ್ಲ) ಬಳಸಿ.

heading.en: At least one? Use 1 minus none

body.en: For three coins, P(at least one head) = 1 − P(no head) = 1 − 1/8 = 7/8. Counting all the "at least one" cases directly is slower and easy to get wrong.

narration.en: At least one? Use 1 minus none. For three coins, P(at least one head) = 1 − P(no head) = 1 − 1/8 = 7/8. Counting all the "at least one" cases directly is slower and easy to get wrong.

narration.en: Recap. P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A ∩ B). Mutually exclusive: P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B). P(A′) = 1 − P(A). At least one = 1 − none.
